_**Agent (grok-4.6)**_

You cannot add **new item kinds** to Paste. You can add **custom content** of the five types it already stores, then label and pin it. That is the whole extension surface.

Assumption from the last turn (`/mcp paste`): “custom items” means Paste history/pinboard items, not a new Cursor skill type. I treated `/find-skills` as “is there a skill for this?” rather than “install something.”

### What an item can be

| Type | How it gets created | MCP `create_item` |
|---|---|---|
| **text** | Copy, Cmd-N, or MCP | Yes (default) |
| **link** | Copy a URL, or MCP if content is a URL | Yes (auto-detect) |
| **color** | Bare 6-digit hex (`#1A2B3C` or `1a2b3c` with A–F) | Yes (auto-detect) |
| **image** | Copy / screenshot | No — copy in-app; MCP can only `read_item` |
| **file** | Copy in Finder | No — copy in-app |

Not item types: `#FFF`, `rgb()`, color names, JSON, snippets-as-a-class, templates-as-a-class. Those stay **text**. Images can be OCR’d and searched in the app; MCP does not create them.

MCP extras that *are* custom: **title** via `update_item` (search label), pin to a **private** pinboard via `list_id`. MCP does **not** write the system clipboard, set pinboard color, or write **shared** pinboards.

Official sources: [What Paste captures](https://pasteapp.io/help/what-paste-captures), [Pinboards](https://pasteapp.io/help/organize-with-pinboards), [Edit and label](https://pasteapp.io/help/edit-items-before-pasting), [Paste MCP](https://pasteapp.io/help/paste-mcp).

### What is worth adding on *your* boards

Live MCP inventory: 31 pinboards. Empty: **deepseek**, **UserScript**. Thin: **prompt** (3), **podCast** (3), **Story** (2), **Json** (2), **LinkedBio** (2), two **Untitled**. **HandOff** has 7 items, all from Nov 2025–Jan 2026 (Claude splash screens, Python rename handoffs) — not current nocturne work.

Highest-value **text** items to author (then `update_item` title, pin):

1. **Identity card** — DSP artist AvaTarArTs, label nocTurneMeLoDies, ID-only identity, no title matching, `spec/identity.json` path. Pin to **Suno** or a new `nocturne-identity` board.
2. **Current HandOff stub** — `HANDOFF_2026-09-13.md`, `suno-1466/STATUS.md`, report command from `MP3/`. Replace the stale HandOff pile rather than mixing years.
3. **Catalog key** — spine CSV name + “UUID = identity, duration confirms only.” Pin to **Suno**.
4. **Reusable Suno style lines** you already copy a lot (`grunge-raccoon acoustic indie-folk`, etc.) — title them so search is not the raw blob.
5. **Safe local paths** as **file** copies (Finder) or path **text**: `spec/identity.json`, the 1477 spine CSV, cover/template files you already copied Oct 10.
6. **Brand hex colors** as **color** items (you already have `#818484`, `#882715`, …) — pin a small nocturne palette instead of leaving them in history.
7. **UserScript / deepseek** — either fill those empty boards with one titled starter snippet each, or delete the empty boards so they stop looking like unfinished custom types.

Do **not** add: API keys, MCP tokens, `.env` contents. History already has an Opera `sk-proj` item from tonight. Paste’s privacy skip does not catch all browser-extension copies.

### `/find-skills`

`npx skills find` for paste/clipboard/pinboard returned **no real match**. Nearby MCP skills on skills.sh are low-install and unrelated (GTM, Jira standup). **Do not install** those. There is no quality public skill that extends Paste item types. Local prior work is `.tmp/paste-history/` (gap analysis 2026-10-11), not a skill.

If you want this as a repeatable agent habit, the right custom artifact is a **local skill** (`npx skills init` / create-skill) that says: search Paste → never echo secrets → create titled text/link/color only → pin to a named private board. That is not an official Paste feature.

Same pass with eza-nav on `/Users/steven/.agent-skills/agents` (`list_all_files.sh -t -d 2`, `/opt/local/bin/eza`). This tree is **not** a skill library. It is mostly **flat agent files**, plus numbered packs.

### Where it sits
| Path | eza |
|---|---|
| `/Users/steven/.agent-skills/agents` | Real dir, `drwx------`, 9 Oct 01:52 |
| `/Users/steven/.agents/` | Exists; **no** `agents/` child |
| `/Users/steven/.Codex/agents` | Real dir, **109 files**, 0 dirs. Sample: `tree-explorer.md` **→** canonical `.md` |
| `/Users/steven/.codex/agents` | Same shape as Codex (109 files) |
| `~/.claude/agents` | 2 files, 6 dirs |
| `~/.cursor/agents` | 32 files, 9 dirs |
| `~/.qwen/agents` | 25 files, 20 dirs |
| `~/.gemini/agents` | 2 files |

Codex is a **runtime door** into this store for at least some `.md` names. Do not treat every Codex `.toml` as a symlink (the listing mixed regular files and links).

### Size
- **243** names at the top
- **12** directories, **231** files
- Files: **113 `.toml`**, **111 `.md`**, 5 csv, 1 yaml, 1 txt
- Root pairing: **110** md+toml pairs; `ARCHIVE-PACKS.md` has no toml; toml-only stems `autotag_architect`, `capability_atlas`, `ecosystem_intelligence` (underscore Gemini-style)

### The 12 directories (packs, not the live flat set)
Numbered packs look like **archives of the same personas** that also sit as root `.md` files. Same *name* is not proof they are the same inode.

| Dir | Role |
|---|---|
| `1-eng-specialist-pack/` | 11 specialist `.md` |
| `2-personal-tooled/` | 9 workflow/tool agents |
| `3-contains-studio/` | 35 studio personas |
| `5-misc-personal/` | 20 personal/ecosystem agents (`tree-explorer.md` lives here **and** at root) |
| `6-automation-workbench/` | 5 agents + README |
| `_incoming/` | 22 category dirs (unmerged intake) |
| `commands/` | 5 command `.md` (`sage`, `hooks-*`, …) |
| `documentation/` | `agent.md` |
| `gemini-roles/` | 3 `*.gemini-agent` |
| `skill-creator/`, `skill-installer/`, `skill-porter/` | skill-packaging **skills nested inside agents/** |

Root also has `AGENT_PATTERN_GUIDE.md`, `MANIFEST.csv`, `agents-meta.csv`, `cleanup-manifest.csv`.

### Paste / clipboard
**No paste, clipboard, or pinboard agent.** Name filter only hit `skill-*` and `tree-explorer`. Body search for Paste.app / clipboard / pinboard was empty. `\bmcp\b` shows up in `_incoming` optimization/v3 drafts and skill-porter — not a Paste consumer.

### Closest agents if you keep exploring this way
- **`tree-explorer.md`** — directory manifests / “what’s in there”
- **`filesystem-inventory.md`**, **`path-list-analyzer.md`** — inventories
- **`sage.md`** + `commands/sage.md` — investigation
- **`skill-creator/`** — how to package a skill, not Paste

`AGENT_PATTERN_GUIDE.md` names three templates: specialist pack, workflow orchestrator, creative generator. A Paste MCP *habit* still belongs in **`skills/`**, not as a new agent, unless you want a coordinator that only dispatches `using-paste-mcp`.

Canonical live definitions for Cursor’s agent list are the **root `*.md` files** here; packs under `1-`…`6-` and `_incoming/` are secondary.

````
Source: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/authorization

Required header for every HTTP request from MCP client to server. The access token must be included in the Authorization header as a Bearer token, conforming to OAuth 2.1 Section 5.1.1.

```http
Authorization: Bearer <access-token>
```

Source: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/utilities/ping

A standard JSON-RPC request with no parameters, used by either the client or server to initiate a ping and verify the counterpart is responsive.

{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": "123",
  "method": "ping"
}

Source: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports

MCP uses JSON-RPC to encode messages. JSON-RPC messages **MUST** be UTF-8 encoded. The protocol currently defines two standard transport mechanisms for client-server communication:
  1. stdio, communication over standard in and standard out
  2. Streamable HTTP

Clients **SHOULD** support stdio whenever possible. It is also possible for clients and servers to implement custom transports in a pluggable fashion.

--------------------------------
````

6. Synthesis / implications  

The working model below is from the **MCP spec 2025-11-25** via Context7 (`/websites/modelcontextprotocol_io_specification_2025-11-25`).

### What MCP is
MCP is an open **JSON-RPC 2.0** protocol so an LLM **host** (Cursor, Claude Code, Codex) can talk to **servers** that expose tools, resources, and prompts. The model never “has MCP.” The host is the client; the server is a subprocess or HTTP service.

### Architecture
| Role | Job |
|---|---|
| **Host** | The app. Owns UI, model calls, which servers you approved. |
| **Client** | One connection inside the host to one server. |
| **Server** | Exposes `tools`, `resources`, `prompts` (and optional utilities). |

Primitives:
- **Tools** — callable actions (`search`, `create_item`, …). That’s what you saw as `user-Paste`.
- **Resources** — readable context (files, URIs). Many servers skip these.
- **Prompts** — named prompt templates the host can offer. Many skip these too.
- **Utilities** — e.g. `ping`.

Messages are UTF-8 JSON-RPC: request, response, or notification.

### Transports (spec current)
The spec defines **two** standard transports:

1. **stdio** — host **launches** the server as a child process. Newline-delimited JSON-RPC on stdin/stdout. stderr is logs only. Nothing else on stdout.
2. **Streamable HTTP** — one MCP HTTP endpoint, POST + GET. Server may use SSE to stream. This **replaced** the old HTTP+SSE transport from 2024-11-05.

Clients should support stdio when they can. Custom transports are allowed.

**Paste MCP** on your Mac is the HTTP/token style (Paste Settings → Intelligence → MCP), not a typical `npx` stdio subprocess. `mcp_auth` is the host’s approval gate onto that local server.

### Auth
On HTTP, the client sends:

```http
Authorization: Bearer <access-token>
```

(OAuth 2.1 bearer, spec § authorization.) Stdio servers usually inherit the user’s local process (no bearer); that’s why Paste’s token warning matters: URL + token = anyone on the machine can call your clipboard.

`ping`:

```json
{ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": "123", "method": "ping" }
```

### How this sits next to skills / hooks / plugins
| Layer | What it is |
|---|---|
| **Skill** | Instructions the model loads (`SKILL.md`). No live clipboard. |
| **Agent** | A persona file under `~/.agent-skills/agents`. |
| **Hook** | Host lifecycle script (SessionStart, PostToolUse, …). |
| **Plugin** | Host package that may **bundle** skills, agents, **and** MCP server defs. |
| **MCP** | Live tools over JSON-RPC. Paste/search/create happen here. |

A skill can tell the model *how* to use Paste MCP; only the MCP connection can actually search pinboards.

Raw DeepTutor dump: `/Users/steven/github/paste-mcp/.tmp/deeptutor-mcp-deep-research.ndjson` (outline only). Spec: [modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports).

Yes. That line was accurate: **RAG was off for that run**, on purpose, because there was nothing to retrieve from.

DeepTutor’s decompose step printed:

`RAG Enabled: False`  
then `RAG is disabled, generating subtopics directly from LLM...`

### Why
In this build, **RAG means “search a knowledge base,”** not “search the web.”

The pipeline has a hard guard (pinned in `test_research_pipeline_rag.py`):

- no `kb_name` → `enable_rag = False`
- a `rag` tool call without a KB returns `skipped` / `no_kb_selected`
- the old fallback KB (`ai_textbook`) was **removed**

This session:

1. `deeptutor kb list` → **No knowledge bases found**
2. The command had **no `--kb`**
3. `--config-json` had `"sources":["papers","web"]` — that is meant to turn on **paper search** and **web search**, which are **not RAG**
4. `deeptutor config show` also fails: **no embedding model** in Settings → Catalog. Even after you create a KB, RAG cannot embed/query until that is set

So decompose sketched six chapters from the model alone and exited. It never retrieved your files, the MCP spec, or papers.

### How to turn RAG on
1. Set an embedding model in DeepTutor Settings → Catalog  
2. Create a KB, e.g. MCP spec + local notes:  
   `deeptutor kb create …`  
3. Pass it:  
   `deeptutor run deep_research "…" --kb <name> --config-json '{"mode":"report","depth":"deep","sources":["kb","web"]}'`

`sources` including `"kb"` without `--kb` will still disable RAG.

I can create an MCP KB from the spec (and optionally `~/.agent-skills` docs) and rerun with RAG on, if you want that next.

```bash
import sqlite3, os
from pathlib import Path

def inspect(p):
    p=Path(p)
    print(f"\n=== {p} size={p.stat().st_size} ===")
    if not p.exists():
        print("MISSING"); return
    try:
        c=sqlite3.connect(f"file:{p}?mode=ro", uri=True)
    except Exception as e:
        print("open fail", e); return
    tables=c.execute("SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' ORDER BY 1").fetchall()
    print("tables:", [t[0] for t in tables])
    for (t,) in tables:
        try:
            n=c.execute(f'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM "{t}"').fetchone()[0]
            cols=[r[1] for r in c.execute(f'PRAGMA table_info("{t}")').fetchall()]
            print(f"  {t}: rows={n} cols={cols[:12]}")
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"  {t}: ERR {e}")

for p in [
    "/Users/steven/.agent-skills/memory/shared.sqlite",
    "/Users/steven/.agent-skills/deeptutor/data/user/chat_history.db",
    "/Users/steven/.grok/memory/steven-dea71e2d/index.sqlite",
]:
    inspect(p)
```

### Host `MEMORY.md` indexes (the real ones)

| Path | Size | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `~/.claude/memory/MEMORY.md` | **26k** | Biggest live index (MCP scoping, skills topology, Engram, hooks) |
| `~/.Codex/memory/MEMORY.md` | 2.4k | Same **inode** as `~/.codex/memory/MEMORY.md` (one file, two names — not a dir symlink) |
| `~/.hermes/memories/MEMORY.md` | 2.2k | mode `600` |
| `~/.qwen/memories/MEMORY.md` | 257b | Plus project copies under `~/.qwen/projects/…/memory/` |
| `~/.grok/memory/MEMORY.md` | 221b | Plus `memory-v2/global` and per-workspace files |
| `~/.gemini/memory/MEMORY.md` | 68b | Almost empty (points at SUPREME_POWERS) |
| `~/.cursor/CHAT_MEMORY.md` | 2.4k | Different **name**; fzf `*memory*.md` caught it |

DeepTutor has **no** `MEMORY.md`. Its session notes are `~/.agent-skills/deeptutor/data/memory/{PROFILE,SUMMARY}.md`.

### SQLite (still not DeepTutor RAG)
- `~/.agent-skills/memory/shared.sqlite` — 100 decisions / 16 patterns / 23 preferences
- `~/.agent-skills/deeptutor/data/user/chat_history.db` — 16 sessions, 2060 turn_events (this is where the MCP outline landed)
- `~/.grok/memory/steven-dea71e2d/index.sqlite` — 8 FTS chunks

None of these markdown indexes or sqlite files are a DeepTutor **KB**. RAG stays off until `deeptutor kb create` + an embedding model in `model_catalog.json`.

Best feed for a later MCP/agents KB: **`~/.claude/memory/MEMORY.md`** plus `reference-mcp-scoping.md` and `reference-agents-skills-topology.md` in that same folder — not the grok marketplace-cache hits.

**Engram** is cloud long-term memory for agents ([getengram.app](https://getengram.app)). **Engram MCP** is the JSON-RPC tool surface onto that cloud. They are not `MEMORY.md`, not DeepTutor RAG, and not Paste.

### What it is
Remote **Streamable HTTP** MCP at `https://mcp.getengram.app/mcp` with a Bearer key. Tools (from `engram-mcp` skill): `search`, `create_conversation`, `append_messages`, `get_conversation`, `list_conversations`, `delete_conversation`, `memory_status`, `whoami`, `manage_subscription`, plus a **vault** (`vault_set/get/list/delete`, `resolve_vault`) for client-encrypted secrets.

Claude’s rule (`~/.claude/rules/engram.md`): file memory (`~/.claude/memory/`) = durable facts; Engram = session history / working context. Search on session start (`limit: 5`). Store decisions, bugs, architecture, preferences — **never secrets in normal messages** (searchable, not encrypted at rest). Vault is the secret store.

CLI `engram` is at `~/.local/bin/engram`. Live status (no key printed): **free plan**, **183 / 10,000** messages, **152 searches** this month.

### This machine
| Piece | State |
|---|---|
| Remote MCP | **Claude user-scope** in `~/.claude.json` (`engram` → getengram.app) |
| Cursor | **`~/.cursor/mcp.json` has no engram** — this session’s tool catalog has **zero** Engram tools |
| Skill | `~/.agent-skills/skills/engram-mcp/` (`SKILL.md` + `scripts/call-tool.py`) |
| Local daemon | **Dead.** pidfile `46905`, no process. Last log **2026-08-08**: `better-sqlite3` missing for **Node ABI 147** (`node-v147-darwin-x64`). Homebrew path is **0.5.0**, not the 0.3.4 note in Claude memory — same crash. Do not trust `engram start` until native rebuild |
| Config dir | `~/.engram/{config.json,daemon.log,daemon.pid}` — keys live there / `~/.env.d/engram.env`; not opened here |

Claude memory `reference-engram-setup.md` is still right on the **shape** (remote MCP works, daemon does not); the brew version in that note is stale.

### Vs the other memory layers
| Store | Role |
|---|---|
| Host `MEMORY.md` | Local indexes (Claude’s 26k file is the dense one) |
| `shared.sqlite` | Cross-skill decisions/patterns on disk |
| DeepTutor RAG | Needs a **KB + embedding catalog** — unrelated |

description: >-
  Use when the agent needs access to Engram MCP tools. Available tools: append_messages, create_conversation, delete_conversation, get_conversation, list_conversations, manage_subscription, memory_status, resolve_vault, search, vault_delete, and 4 more.

# Engram Tools

## How to Call Tools

```bash
python3 scripts/call-tool.py <tool_name> '<arguments_json>'
```

## Tools

### append_messages

Saves messages to the user's long-term memory, making them available in future sessions in this app and any other AI the user connects. Applicable when the user asks to remember or save something (a preference, a fact, a decision, a goal, project context), or under a standing request from the user to keep saving as the conversation continues. Stores messages verbatim, auto-chunked + embedded for search. conversation_id is optional: omit it to append to the user's default memory, or set it to group messages under a specific conversation. The response returns the conversation_id used. Stores only the messages passed in — it cannot fetch past or external chat history (bulk import is separate, via the Engram CLI). Not suitable for secrets (passwords, API keys, tokens, government IDs): stored text is searchable and resurfaces in future context; Engram's separate zero-knowledge encrypted vault is the store for credentials. Optionally accepts client-encrypted vault entries.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| conversation_id | string | No | Optional. Omit to append to the user's default memory; set to group messages under a specific conversation. |
| messages | array<object> | Yes | Messages to append |
| vault_entries | array<object> | No | Client-encrypted vault entries. Server stores these as opaque blobs — zero knowledge. |

**Example:**
```bash
python3 scripts/call-tool.py append_messages '{"conversation_id":"...","messages":[],"vault_entries":[]}'
```

---

### create_conversation

Create a new conversation and return its conversation_id, used to group subsequently appended messages under one topic. Memory is scoped to the user's account; on multi-seat team accounts, a stored conversation is visible to the whole team by default and can be restricted to its creator with visibility 'private'.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| agent_id | string | No | Agent identifier (e.g. "chatgpt") |
| metadata | object | No | Arbitrary metadata |
| tags | array<string> | No | Tags for filtering |
| title | string | No | Title for the conversation |
| visibility | string | No | Team accounts: 'private' keeps this conversation visible only to the seat that created it. Default 'shared' (org-wide). |

**Example:**
```bash
python3 scripts/call-tool.py create_conversation '{"agent_id":"...","metadata":{},"tags":[],"title":"...","visibility":"..."}'
```

---

### delete_conversation

Delete a conversation and all its messages, chunks, and vector embeddings.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| conversation_id | string | Yes | The conversation to delete |

**Example:**
```bash
python3 scripts/call-tool.py delete_conversation '{"conversation_id":"..."}'
```

---

### get_conversation

Get a conversation with its full verbatim messages. Supports pagination.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| conversation_id | string | Yes | The conversation to retrieve |
| message_limit | integer | No | Max messages to return |
| message_offset | integer | No | Message offset for pagination |

**Example:**
```bash
python3 scripts/call-tool.py get_conversation '{"conversation_id":"...","message_limit":0,"message_offset":0}'
```

---

### list_conversations

List conversations with filtering and sorting options.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| agent_id | string | No | Filter by agent ID |
| limit | integer | No | - |
| offset | integer | No | - |
| order | string | No | - |
| sort | string | No | - |
| tags | array<string> | No | Filter by tags |

**Example:**
```bash
python3 scripts/call-tool.py list_conversations '{"agent_id":"...","limit":0,"offset":0,"order":"...","sort":"...","tags":[]}'
```

---

### manage_subscription

View your current subscription or get a link to upgrade/manage your plan. Returns a Stripe Checkout URL for upgrades or a billing portal URL for existing subscribers. IMPORTANT: When this tool returns a URL, you MUST open it in the user's browser by running `open <url>` (macOS) or `xdg-open <url>` (Linux) — do not just display the URL as text.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| action | string | No | "status" — show current tier and limits. "upgrade" — get a checkout link to subscribe to Pro or Team. "portal" — get a link to manage an existing subscription. |
| plan | string | No | Target plan for upgrade. Defaults to "pro". Only used with action "upgrade". |
| quantity | number | No | Number of seats for team plan. Only used with action "upgrade" and plan "team". |

**Example:**
```bash
python3 scripts/call-tool.py manage_subscription '{"action":"...","plan":"...","quantity":0}'
```

---

### memory_status

Show how full the user's Engram memory is: lifetime storage used vs the plan's capacity, plus a monthly meter on plans that have one. Returns a ready-to-display progress bar string.

No parameters required.

**Example:**
```bash
python3 scripts/call-tool.py memory_status '{}'
```

---

### resolve_vault

Retrieve encrypted vault entries by ID. Returns encrypted blobs — decryption happens client-side.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| vault_ids | array<string> | Yes | Vault entry IDs to resolve (e.g. vlt_abc123) |

**Example:**
```bash
python3 scripts/call-tool.py resolve_vault '{"vault_ids":[]}'
```

---

### search

Searches the user's long-term memory. Applicable when previously saved context is relevant to the current request — for example when the user references something from before ('what did we decide', 'like last time', 'my usual', a project/person/preference by name) or asks what is remembered about a topic. Hybrid search (semantic + keyword) across stored conversations. Each result includes a short chunk_summary, the full chunk_text snippet, conversation_title, tags, and relevance scores, best match first.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| conversation_id | string | No | Limit search to a specific conversation |
| limit | integer | No | Max results (default 5) |
| project | string | No | Filter by project name (matches conversation title prefix, case-insensitive). Use to avoid cross-project noise. |
| query | string | Yes | Search query text |
| tags | array<string> | No | Filter by conversation tags |

**Example:**
```bash
python3 scripts/call-tool.py search '{"conversation_id":"...","limit":0,"project":"...","query":"...","tags":[]}'
```

---

### vault_delete

Delete a named secret permanently. This action cannot be undone.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| name | string | Yes | Secret name to delete |

**Example:**
```bash
python3 scripts/call-tool.py vault_delete '{"name":"..."}'
```

---

### vault_get

Retrieve a named secret's encrypted blob. Decryption happens client-side with your vault key.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| name | string | Yes | Secret name to retrieve (e.g. DATABASE_URL) |

**Example:**
```bash
python3 scripts/call-tool.py vault_get '{"name":"..."}'
```

---

### vault_list

List all named secrets. Returns names and metadata only — never values or encrypted blobs.

No parameters required.

**Example:**
```bash
python3 scripts/call-tool.py vault_list '{}'
```

---

### vault_set

Store a named secret. The value must be encrypted client-side before calling this tool. The server stores the encrypted blob — it never sees plaintext.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| encrypted_value | string | Yes | Base64-encoded AES-256-GCM ciphertext |
| iv | string | Yes | Base64-encoded initialization vector |
| name | string | Yes | Secret name (e.g. DATABASE_URL, OPENAI_KEY) |
| secret_type | string | No | Type of secret (e.g. api_key, connection_string, token) |

**Example:**
```bash
python3 scripts/call-tool.py vault_set '{"encrypted_value":"...","iv":"...","name":"...","secret_type":"..."}'
```

---

### whoami

Show which Engram account this connection is using — organization name, email, tier, and how you are authenticated. Use when unsure which account memories are being saved to or searched from.

No parameters required.

**Example:**
```bash
python3 scripts/call-tool.py whoami '{}'
```

```bash
python3 - <<'PY'
import json
from pathlib import Path
from datetime import datetime

cursor_path = Path.home() / '.cursor' / 'mcp.json'
claude_path = Path.home() / '.claude.json'

cursor = json.loads(cursor_path.read_text())
claude = json.loads(claude_path.read_text())
eng = (claude.get('mcpServers') or {}).get('engram')
if not eng:
    raise SystemExit('no engram server in ~/.claude.json')

servers = cursor.setdefault('mcpServers', {})
if 'engram' in servers:
    print('ALREADY_PRESENT keys=', sorted(servers['engram'].keys()))
else:
    bak = cursor_path.with_suffix('.json.bak-' + datetime.now().strftime('%Y%m%d-%H%M%S'))
    bak.write_text(cursor_path.read_text())
    # Cursor style: url + headers (match vidIQ/Paste), not Claude's extra "type"
    entry = {
        'url': eng['url'],
        'headers': dict(eng.get('headers') or {}),
    }
    servers['engram'] = entry
    cursor_path.write_text(json.dumps(cursor, indent=2) + '\n')
    print('ADDED_ENGRAM')
    print('backup', bak)

# verify without printing secrets
cur2 = json.loads(cursor_path.read_text())
e = cur2['mcpServers']['engram']
auth = (e.get('headers') or {}).get('Authorization', '')
print('url', e.get('url'))
print('auth_present', auth.startswith('Bearer ') and len(auth) > 20)
print('server_names', list(cur2['mcpServers'].keys()))
PY
```

````
### Create a Streamable HTTP endpoint in Express

Source: https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/blob/main/packages/middleware/express/README.md

Handle incoming MCP requests statelessly on an Express POST route using McpServer and NodeStreamableHTTPServerTransport.

```typescript
import { createMcpExpressApp } from '@modelcontextprotocol/express';
import { NodeStreamableHTTPServerTransport } from '@modelcontextprotocol/node';
import { McpServer } from '@modelcontextprotocol/server';

const app = createMcpExpressApp();

app.post('/mcp', async (req, res) => {
    // Stateless example: create a server and a transport per request (with sessions: one pair per session).
    const server = new McpServer({ name: 'my-server', version: '1.0.0' });
    const transport = new NodeStreamableHTTPServerTransport({ sessionIdGenerator: undefined });
    await server.connect(transport);
    await transport.handleRequest(req, res, req.body);
});
```

Source: https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/blob/main/docs/servers/errors.md
````
